title: Circuit fooling condition
statement: Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $S$ be a set of Boolean circuits on $n$ inputs. The set $S$ is fooled with error $\varepsilon$ by $k$-wise independent distributions if, for every $k$-wise independent probability distribution $\mu$ on Boolean assignments to the inputs and every $C\in S$, the absolute difference between the probability that $C$ accepts under $\mu$ and its acceptance probability under the uniform distribution on all input assignments is at most $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: A set $S$ of circuits on $n$ inputs
Every $k$-wise independent distribution on Boolean assignments to the inputs
caveat: The supplied formal snippet does not define the notation $C.\mathrm{prob}\,\mu$; the statement interprets it as the probability that the circuit evaluates to true under $\mu$. The snippet also does not impose a sign condition on $\varepsilon$.
